title: Packaging and Label Inspection
summary: Camera checks on cartons, labels and blister foils that verify batch, expiry, MRP and codes, compare print against approved artwork, and reject mismatches with image evidence.

seo.title: AI Pharma Packaging and Label Inspection | VipraTech
seo.description: Vision system that verifies batch, expiry, MRP and codes on pharma cartons and labels, compares print with approved artwork and logs evidence.

problem.intro: Labelling and packaging errors are a common reason for product recalls. Every carton, label and foil carries variable data printed on the line, such as batch number, manufacturing and expiry dates, MRP and often a QR code or barcode, and operators check samples by eye. Artwork changes add a second risk upstream.

pain_points.title: Variable data printed wrong
pain_points.detail: Smudged, missing or wrong batch and expiry overprint, often after a changeover, can pass a periodic visual check.

pain_points.title: Artwork version errors
pain_points.detail: An outdated carton or leaflet version reaching the line, or a text change missed in proofreading, affects the whole batch.

pain_points.title: Unreadable or wrong codes
pain_points.detail: QR codes and barcodes needed for track-and-trace or Indian labelling rules must scan correctly and must encode the right data.

pain_points.title: Thin evidence of checks
pain_points.detail: Manual line checks leave little beyond a signed checklist when an auditor or customer asks how a defect escaped.

solution.overview: We build vision inspection for carton, label and foil lines. Cameras capture each unit; the system reads the overprinted batch, dates and MRP, checks them against the batch details set at line clearance, decodes and grades the QR code or barcode, and compares the printed layout with the approved artwork. A separate proofing tool compares a new artwork PDF with the previous approved version and highlights every text, colour and layout change for the labelling team. Units that fail trigger the line's reject mechanism, and each rejection is stored with its image and reason.
capabilities: Reads batch number, manufacturing and expiry dates and MRP on cartons, labels and blister foils
Verifies printed data against the batch details set at line clearance
Decodes and grades QR codes, Data Matrix and linear barcodes, and checks their content
Compares each printed unit with the approved artwork to catch wrong or mixed components
Proofs new artwork PDFs against the previous approved version and lists every change
Stores an image and reason for every rejected unit, linked to the batch

workflow.title: Set up the batch
workflow.detail: At line clearance the operator scans the batch order, and the station loads expected batch data and the approved artwork reference.

workflow.title: Capture each unit
workflow.detail: Cameras triggered by the line sensor capture every carton, label or foil at line speed.

workflow.title: Read and verify
workflow.detail: Variable data is read, codes are decoded and graded, and the layout is compared with the reference.

workflow.title: Accept or reject
workflow.detail: Units that fail any check are rejected by the line mechanism; uncertain reads are rejected too and counted separately.

workflow.title: Operator and QA review
workflow.detail: The operator reviews reject images, and repeated failures stop the line for QA investigation.

workflow.title: Batch inspection report
workflow.detail: At batch end, counts, reject reasons and sample images are compiled for the batch packaging record.

inputs: Batch order with batch number, dates and MRP
Approved artwork PDFs for cartons, labels, foils and leaflets
Camera images from the packaging line
Rules for expected QR code or barcode content
outputs: Accept or reject decision per unit
Artwork change report for new versions
Batch-level inspection summary for the BPR
human_in_the_loop: Operators review rejected units, and QA investigates repeated failures before the line restarts. The labelling team approves every artwork change the proofing tool highlights, and QA approves any change to inspection recipes.
integrations: ERP or MES for batch orders
Line PLC for triggers and rejects
Serialisation or track-and-trace system where in use
QMS for deviations raised from inspection failures
guardrails: Uncertain reads treated as rejects, never as passes
Challenge test with known defective samples at batch start and end
Inspection recipes locked and changed only through change control
Every reject image retained with batch and timestamp
Line stop after repeated consecutive rejects for investigation
compliance_notes: Supports labelling controls under GMP, including India's revised Schedule M, and the QR code or barcode requirements in Indian labelling rules for APIs and specified brands.
Inspection software and recipes are validated as a GMP computerised system, with audit trails aligned to 21 CFR Part 11 and EU GMP Annex 11.

pilot.scope: One carton or label line for one product family, starting with offline images from earlier runs and moving to an in-line station that logs rejects without actuating them.
deliverables: Camera and lighting specification for the line
Verification and artwork models set up for the pilot SKUs
Challenge test set with known defects
Inspection report comparing system results with manual checks

what_we_measure.how: Known defective samples, such as wrong batch or missing expiry, run through the station in challenge tests.
Rejected units that operator review finds acceptable, counted per batch.
Printed values read by the system compared with the batch order for every unit captured.
Known differences between artwork versions checked against what the proofing tool reports.

faqs.q: We already have OCR and OCV cameras. What is different?
faqs.a: Many lines have vendor OCR for one or two fields. We add artwork comparison, code content checks and a batch-level evidence trail, and can work alongside existing cameras where their images are accessible.

faqs.q: Can it keep up with our line speed?
faqs.a: Models run on an edge PC next to the line, and the pilot measures processing time per unit at your actual speed. Camera and trigger choice depends on line speed and is specified during the pilot.

faqs.q: How do you add new SKUs?
faqs.a: Each new SKU needs its approved artwork and variable-data layout loaded, followed by a short challenge test. This runs under your change control procedure.
The proofing tool compares leaflet artwork PDFs version to version. In-line leaflet inspection depends on how the leaflet is presented on your line, which we assess during the pilot.
